entities.summary: Baron Vilmos Apor de Altorja was a Hungarian Roman Catholic prelate, born as a baron in the noble Apor family, and served as a bishop during World War II. He became famous for protesting against the persecution of the Hungarian Jewish population and for his steadfast commitment to the poor. His outreach also extended to abuse victims with a particular emphasis on the protection of women - it would be this latter commitment that saw him sustain fatal injuries leading to his death. Apor dedicated himself to being an opponent of both communism and Nazism and used his sermons as a platform to condemn them though coming at a great personal risk to himself.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a vocal opponent of Nazism and communism, Vilmos Apor's sermons played a significant role in shaping Hungarian public opinion during World War II. His commitment to protecting the poor and abuse victims led to his tragic death, but also cemented his legacy as a champion of human rights.
